blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse, tuned for Omnichannel Retail: sector-specific design decisions, the delivery pattern with named owners, and outcomes gated on signed metrics.

Omnichannel retail wins on promise-keeping: availability, delivery promise, price consistency and service resolution across channels. The decision infrastructure behind those promises — demand sensing, allocation, pricing — decides margin before marketing spends a cent.

items: Forecasts update weekly while baskets shift daily; markdowns and stockouts both inherit the lag.
Store/DC allocation on legacy rules; phantom availability coexists with overstock.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Data Monetization & Analytics Products, Enterprise BI & Executive Analytics, Data Monetization & Analytics Products from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Demand sensing and pricing, Allocation/replenishment, Order promise and fulfillment) on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — GDPR/CCPA among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Resilient, observable pipelines: trusted data from source to decision at SLA.
Lakehouse the right way: Unity Catalog governance, cost-aware design and AI-ready foundations.
Decisions at event speed: sub-second pipelines from sensor, click or transaction to action.
Streaming signals into daily SKU-store forecasts (forecast error down 20-35%)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Retail & Consumer Goods level this capability reads as: POS, loyalty, supply and cost data unified for merchandising and finance (margin bridge decomposes automatically). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Every program of this type runs the same weekly rhythm, so your team can plan around it. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
